Record epsilon and use the same baseline version for correction inputs, ratio targets, and output multiplication. Do not update the first-stage model while claiming second-stage-only training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An observed 10 seconds divided by a 0.01-second baseline creates a huge factor that is not necessarily reliable preference evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17863">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.17863-dadf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea006a6d3351f5f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:danet" data-paper-title="Cheaper is Better: A Discount-Aware Network for Conversion Rate Prediction in E-commerce Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-danet-112ada17" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f4d3b95fcfb94c4">Why model general interest and discount preference separately in DANet?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adanet">Cheaper is Better: A Discount-Aware Network for Conversion Rate Prediction in E-commerce Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Category interest is not the same as willingness to wait for discounts. IPN models general interest, DPN learns discount rhythms, and user and promotion context modulate them. The signals can interact but are not interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two sneaker fans may buy at full price or wait for a season-end sale despite similar browsing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12578">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12578-danet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f4d3b95fcfb94c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:danet" data-paper-title="Cheaper is Better: A Discount-Aware Network for Conversion Rate Prediction in E-commerce Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-10d7141209c02687">Why does DANet separate high- and low-frequency discount history rather than using only today&#x27;s discount?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adanet">Cheaper is Better: A Discount-Aware Network for Conversion Rate Prediction in E-commerce Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current price cannot describe long-term sensitivity and short-term promotion reactions. DPN separates stable patterns from fast variations and modulates preferences with similar purchases and promotion context; another network models general interest. Purchase-only discount labels are auxiliary and do not identify causal effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two users see 20% off, but one shops only during annual events and the other reacts to regular small offers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12578">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12578-danet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10d7141209c02687">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:danet" data-paper-title="Cheaper is Better: A Discount-Aware Network for Conversion Rate Prediction in E-commerce Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a3d1093600eb1bc">What structure does DANet&#x27;s FFT frequency decomposition preserve beyond a recent discount average?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adanet">Cheaper is Better: A Discount-Aware Network for Conversion Rate Prediction in E-commerce Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A mean compresses trends and fluctuations into one number. Frequency separation reveals promotion rhythm, but depends on temporal sampling and quality, and high frequencies can be noise. Public data without prices provide proxy diagnostics only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Steady 10% off with a rare 50% sale can average similarly to weekly swings between 20% off and full price, but behavior can differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12578">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12578-danet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a3d1093600eb1bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:danet" data-paper-title="Cheaper is Better: A Discount-Aware Network for Conversion Rate Prediction in E-commerce Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-55f9897e4488e735">Why does DANet regress observed discounts only on purchases?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adanet">Cheaper is Better: A Discount-Aware Network for Conversion Rate Prediction in E-commerce Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target is a transaction discount conditioned on purchase, which unpurchased items lack. Mask with purchase positives rather than inventing labels. After FFT filtering, low-frequency reconstruction plus high-frequency residual should recover the sequence. Local popularity/rating intensity is not real coupon-price regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unpurchased shoe has no transaction discount; do not assign it zero. Use actual purchase discounts for this head and separate click or ranking supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12578">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12578-danet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-55f9897e4488e735">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dceo" data-paper-title="DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dceo-b39ed1b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1685d471a4a64785">What do DCEO&#x27;s actor and user-level critic each do?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adceo">DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The actor gives contextual weights to fuse click, conversion, and value scores immediately. The critic estimates the action&#x27;s relative long-term effects during training. Serving keeps only the actor; that does not validate critic causality assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The critic checks whether a shift from relevance toward transaction value yields incremental long-term benefit without running that evaluator at serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25635">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.25635-dceo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1685d471a4a64785">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dceo" data-paper-title="DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-58453392f6b5bfe3">Why does DCEO use an actor to output contextual objective weights instead of one sitewide CTR/CVR/GMV mix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adceo">DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weights assume identical trade-offs across user states. The actor emits dynamic weights summing to one; the critic assesses relative intervention effects in training while serving uses the lightweight actor. Dynamic weights do not establish causal identification without credible controls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Exploration may matter for a new user and conversion for a mature shopper, but compare appropriate long-term feedback rather than just clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25635">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.25635-dceo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58453392f6b5bfe3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dceo" data-paper-title="DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e19239d99d64438">What does DCEO&#x27;s dynamic simplex weighting add over fixed log fusion, and what are its risks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adceo">DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonnegative weights summing to one can express different trade-offs per request. More flexibility can overfit or exploit proxy rewards, requiring validation and per-objective checks. Local Hit rose but NDCG fell slightly, so this is not a clean sweep.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Pushing popular items forward can raise hits while degrading positions of relevant items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25635">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.25635-dceo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e19239d99d64438">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dceo" data-paper-title="DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fcb3cc13628fc19">Why does local DCEO run the held-out test only once for the validation champion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adceo">DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>`causal_gain` and temperature define 20 candidate configurations evaluated only on fixed validation utility. Test only the selected champion to avoid using test variation as search feedback. Public proxy scores and the method&#x27;s causal name are not evidence of real intervention effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Testing all 20 and taking the highest converts test into validation. Lock the champion first and report any NDCG regression honestly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25635">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.25635-dceo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fcb3cc13628fc19">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:easq" data-paper-title="Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-easq-454991cc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-23ddce3a069d0d93">Why separate survey satisfaction and behavior feedback parameter paths in EASQ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeasq">Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior is plentiful but can reflect short-lived clicks; surveys are direct but sparse. Separate LoRA protects satisfaction learning and supplies a preference reference. Survey response bias remains, so these are not unbiased population labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clicks followed by reported regret can be drowned out in pooled updates but remain influential through an independent expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20215">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.20215-easq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-23ddce3a069d0d93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:easq" data-paper-title="Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f5d8831db260b0a">Why give sparse EASQ survey satisfaction a separate LoRA path and dynamic reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeasq">Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Abundant behavior labels can swamp direct but sparse satisfaction signals. A separate low-rank path preserves survey expertise; online preference optimization uses it as a changing reference instead of chasing clicks alone. This reduces interference, not survey selection bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Curiosity clicks can coexist with dissatisfaction in a few surveys, which remain influential through a dedicated expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20215">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.20215-easq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f5d8831db260b0a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:easq" data-paper-title="Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-120b292fc590341a">How does a dynamic survey reference differ from a fixed SFT reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeasq">Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The fixed reference anchors to the initial distribution, while the survey expert adapts to newer satisfaction evidence. A moving reference is nonstationary and needs versions and limits. Updates need not always improve it, and LoRA alone does not prove backbone retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A newer expert can reflect growing dislike of repetitive content, while a fixed reference may keep rewarding stale behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20215">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.20215-easq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-120b292fc590341a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:easq" data-paper-title="Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-09ba941e97be607b">Why verify actual trainable parameters for EASQ rather than checking only a LoRA configuration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeasq">Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the optimizer updates the backbone, the run is not an independent low-rank path for sparse satisfaction. Reference probabilities must match recorded versions, and serving dependencies must agree with training. A public proxy without surveys is not satisfaction reproduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Full backbone updates can lower loss without proving LoRA protected ranking; inspect gradients and optimizer groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20215">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.20215-easq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09ba941e97be607b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ektm" data-paper-title="Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ektm-e47d7330" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-37226c0f09f37dfc">Why transfer CTR knowledge into multiple EKTM CVR tasks instead of learning each from scratch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aektm">Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense clicks can give relevance and interest knowledge to sparse conversions, but tasks differ. Similarity controls borrowing and hard-example loss limits harmful transfer. Measure each target separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cart and purchase can share interest signals, while returns mean something different; both zero transfer and indiscriminate transfer have risks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05730-ektm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-37226c0f09f37dfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ektm" data-paper-title="Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e3e011f83fa003d">Why does EKTM transfer CTR features by task similarity rather than sharing equally across conversions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aektm">Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Click labels are plentiful but relate differently to each conversion. Similarity controls transfer strength, hard-example supervision reduces negative transfer, and CVR towers retain their own targets. Validate similarities; abundant CTR data are not universally trustworthy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cart additions may relate closely to clicks while long-term renewal depends on other factors, so they should not inherit the same strength.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05730-ektm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e3e011f83fa003d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ektm" data-paper-title="Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2517233fca0a5f4d">Where does EKTM control conflicts compared with a shared-bottom model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aektm">Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared-bottom uses the same backbone for all tasks. EKTM weights task-specific contributions during transfer and constrains harmful sharing with hard examples. This adds conditional specialization, similarity dependence, and tower cost; a movie proxy does not prove conversion improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A purchase tower can borrow more from add-to-cart knowledge than an unrelated tower instead of competing for an identical shared representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05730-ektm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2517233fca0a5f4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ektm" data-paper-title="Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a265bd597f40dca1">Why verify task identity, not only shape, when EKTM combines fctr and weighted CVR features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aektm">Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each similarity weight is tied to a source-target task and vectors must be semantically aligned. Preserve ordering mappings and derive hard-example masks from valid labels, never test scores. Public proxies do not create missing production conversion labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A CTR-to-purchase weight can multiply a favorites tower without a shape error, yet corrupt supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05730-ektm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a265bd597f40dca1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:esmm" data-paper-title="Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-esmm-4cd7f113" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be460592e37829a5">Why is CTCVR defined on all ESMM impressions but conditional CVR is not?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aesmm">Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonclicks are known negatives for click-and-convert, but whether they would convert if clicked is unobserved. The CTR–CVR product enables full-space joint supervision only under nested click-to-conversion semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unclicked ad did not produce a post-click purchase, but this says nothing definitive about purchase under a click.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be460592e37829a5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:esmm" data-paper-title="Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb787df90c5dc8be">Why train CTR and CTCVR in ESMM rather than treating nonclicks as CVR negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aesmm">Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CVR is conditional on clicking; no click does not reveal post-click purchase. CTR × CVR represents click-and-convert probability, enabling full-impression CTR and joint supervision to address sparsity and selection. The probability chain does not solve attribution, delayed feedback, or causal identification automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>10% CTR and 20% CVR give 2% joint rate. A nonclick labels click and joint events zero but cannot label hypothetical post-click conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb787df90c5dc8be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:esmm" data-paper-title="Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d59e37d79697e99">What impression information does ESMM add beyond CVR learned only in clicked space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aesmm">Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clicked examples reflect user selection and the prior policy. Full-space CTR and CTCVR let nonclicks constrain joint outcomes, and shared features help sparse conversion. Neither AUC nor full-space supervision resolves delayed feedback or all confounding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Skipped expensive phones supply impression information, not direct counterfactual conversions if clicked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d59e37d79697e99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:esmm" data-paper-title="Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-66950367b1602236">Which ESMM losses use nonclicks, and which head should not be directly supervised by them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aesmm">Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-impression click labels supervise CTR; full-impression CTCVR labels supervise CTR × CVR. Do not add direct CVR negatives for nonclicks. The local rating-threshold nesting validates wiring, not real ad conversions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A nonclick can lower joint probability via low CTR. Forcing CVR to zero adds an unsupported conditional label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66950367b1602236">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:flvm" data-paper-title="Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-flvm-33286ec7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-17e1de9e754f07eb">Why separate consumption, active engagement, and direction in FLVM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aflvm">Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Watching, acting, and liking are different, and negative feedback can be highly active. Restricted heads use relevant factors rather than counting all engagement positively. Latents do not automatically identify psychological concepts and require semantic checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finishing a controversial video and disliking it gives high consumption and engagement but low positive direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32839">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-17e1de9e754f07eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:flvm" data-paper-title="Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-63ac9135b7c263d4">Why does FLVM place measurement confounders in a restricted baseline and correct feedback heads through routed latents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aflvm">Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Watch time reflects length and user habits, not pure preference. The baseline explains measurement conditions; separate consumption, active engagement, and polarity factors reach only relevant heads. Stop-gradient prevents the residual objective from rewriting its reference. These constraints do not fully identify causal latents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar watched seconds can come from completing a short clip or abandoning a long one; length opportunity and active liking should not become one score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32839">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63ac9135b7c263d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:flvm" data-paper-title="Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a996c425104773c4">What shortcut do FLVM&#x27;s constrained baseline and stop-gradient restrict compared with a shared multitask tower?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aflvm">Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Duration and time first explain the measurement baseline. Full user-item information contributes via latents and fixed semantic routing, while baseline gradients train separately. This limits unrestricted mixing but does not remove all confounding; local factor separation was not stable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Let length explain greater opportunity to accumulate seconds, rather than using long as a direct synonym for liked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32839">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a996c425104773c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:flvm" data-paper-title="Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c10ba9bb3d066ce">Why distinguish FLVM feedback masks from fixed latent routing masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aflvm">Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observation masks indicate whether sample labels exist; routing masks restrict which factors heads read, on different axes. Missing labels are not zero, baseline addition stops the specified gradients, and ranking uses the defined combination of consumption and polarity rather than rewarding activity as positive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unobserved dislike is not a like. Even when observed, a dislike head cannot read unrelated factors to bypass routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32839">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c10ba9bb3d066ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gpl-prerank" data-paper-title="Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gpl-prerank-737de503" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3057b5a728b7bb76">Why does GPL target unexposed candidates rather than only adding more exposed-click logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agpl-prerank">Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Renmin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The preranker sees a wider pool than final exposure. Interest anchors and LLM weak labels broaden supervision toward retrieval distribution. Inferred labels cannot replace all observed feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If ten out of 1,000 retrieved items are displayed, the remaining items are not necessarily bad; weak relevance labels do not establish positive user feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20995">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.20995-gpl-prerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3057b5a728b7bb76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gpl-prerank" data-paper-title="Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b23a16668d0204b">Why add pseudolabels for unexposed candidates in GPL pre-ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agpl-prerank">Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Renmin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exposed click examples were selected by the old system and omit many early rejects. An LLM supplies additional labels based on user interest anchors, while a lightweight preranker serves. These noisy judgments are not counterfactual truth; control weight and measure bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A relevant new category may have no logged clicks because it was never shown; estimated relevance does not mean users bought or liked it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20995">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.20995-gpl-prerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b23a16668d0204b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gpl-prerank" data-paper-title="Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4251d480d33b6f86">What assumption does GPL pseudolabeling address compared with labeling all nonexposures negative?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agpl-prerank">Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Renmin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Missing opportunity is not rejection. Weak labels estimate relevance from intent but can transfer LLM bias; weight them and keep real labels. Removing the LLM from serving does not prove label quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unseen waterproof shoe can get a weak positive from an interest anchor, yet persuasive ad copy can still fool the teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20995">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.20995-gpl-prerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4251d480d33b6f86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gpl-prerank" data-paper-title="Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6c7b39eceaa12bb">Why record GPL real and pseudo supervision sources and λ separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agpl-prerank">Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Renmin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Labels differ in reliability and coverage, and the joint coefficient controls pseudo-example influence. Keep provenance; use available history only and exclude test targets from anchors. Public proxies do not reproduce the production LLM labeling system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten thousand weak labels can overwhelm 100 real clicks if equally weighted; source and weight make that auditable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
