<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hge" data-paper-title="Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hge-0554c3a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c32f38715552fb0a">Are HGE&#x27;s top-K items the displayed recommendations or inputs within one container?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahge">Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They are item inputs for each candidate store or room. Set attention models internal relations and combines user/query context to score the container. Top-K is partial inventory, not a list of K stores or item outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three internal products from each of two stores yield six encoded items but only two store scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32420v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.32420-hge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c32f38715552fb0a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hge" data-paper-title="Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5741411042653d97">Why does HGE separately predict container conversion, conditional item purchases, and quantities instead of one store GMV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahge">Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Aggregate GMV is sparse and noisy. Decompose transaction probability and conditional item contributions, with residuals for top-K omissions. Items are not mutually exclusive, and the fusion gate uses context rather than realized conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shopper can buy two inexpensive items or one expensive item; one categorical choice cannot represent both patterns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32420v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.32420-hge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5741411042653d97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hge" data-paper-title="Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-96dc7e4b12d4bae4">Why do HGE item sigmoid and mutually exclusive softmax imply different business assumptions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahge">Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A transaction can contain multiple items, so independent sigmoid scores can all be high. Softmax forces one distribution with a fixed sum and changes basket semantics. Quantity is a distinct head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Buying coffee and bread together should not require the probability of bread to fall when coffee increases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32420v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.32420-hge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96dc7e4b12d4bae4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hge" data-paper-title="Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18f65c0f1ef11458">Why must HGE not select residual and fusion branches using realized conversion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahge">Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residuals can correct over- and underestimation and need not be nonnegative. Predict gates from pre-impression context, not observed transaction labels. The component lacks full multitask training, and differentiating squared output is a gradient diagnostic only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Using the decomposition only after learning a store converted leaks the answer and inflates test results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32420v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.32420-hge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18f65c0f1ef11458">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:incrementality" data-paper-title="From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-incrementality-26b16fde" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a5953a5c0b25bb74">Why does Incrementality define the value of outreach as μ1−μ0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aincrementality">From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>μ1 estimates the outcome under treatment and μ0 without it. Their difference distinguishes what the action creates from what would happen anyway. Give scarce capacity to people whose behavior can change, not merely those likely to respond. The two potential outcomes cannot be observed together, so estimation needs support and identification assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A would buy without a message; B changes their choice only with one. A high treated purchase rate does not imply high incremental value, so it is not enough to rank by that outcome alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a5953a5c0b25bb74">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:incrementality" data-paper-title="From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b37a9687331955">Why might a likely buyer not be the best target under a limited outreach budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aincrementality">From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy cares about how much taking the action changes the outcome. High purchase probability may mean the user would buy without outreach. The method estimates treated and untreated outcomes and allocates the budget by uplift after an uncertainty penalty. A credible difference needs experimental support and identification conditions; two prediction heads alone do not make it causal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A often buys either way, while B may buy only after seeing a relevant recommendation. B&#x27;s raw purchase rate can be lower while B provides more incremental value for the same outreach slot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4b37a9687331955">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:incrementality" data-paper-title="From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcfc9a80acae26bd">How does allocating by τ−λσ differ from ranking by mean uplift alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aincrementality">From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The uncertainty penalty deprioritizes poorly supported, possibly overestimated candidates and favors robust budget value. A mean-only policy may chase high-variance extremes. The penalty can also miss genuinely promising new groups and is not an exploration policy. A single proxy policy-value estimate cannot settle the trade-off universally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two users have the same estimated uplift, but one has abundant history and the other one response. Conservative allocation prefers the former; active exploration may require a separate budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcfc9a80acae26bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:incrementality" data-paper-title="From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3fa67cab9ff6ef8f">Why should fixed-budget allocation check B but allow some budget to remain unused?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aincrementality">From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The constraint caps actions at B; it does not require all B. If risk-adjusted values are negative, do not send unhelpful messages just to fill the quota. Ranking and allocation must use consistent identities and cutoff features, without selecting people based on future test outcomes. The source&#x27;s fixed-percentage proxy is not real long-term online incrementality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If ten messages are available but only three users have positive risk-adjusted value, sending all ten can lower value. Unless the business explicitly requires it, the constraint does not force full use.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3fa67cab9ff6ef8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:light-heads" data-paper-title="Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-light-heads-bf390928" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-238d80dda721f3d5">Why do Light Heads introduce a shallow head instead of changing the shared backbone immediately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alight-heads">Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A production system can try a new objective quickly while protecting existing tasks and interfaces. The head reads shared features and updates only itself, making a cheap probe. It can exploit but not improve the backbone through this loss, and cannot recover information absent from those features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Probe sparse satisfaction on current user embeddings without changing the click network. Adding a head cannot conjure details the embeddings never captured.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25433">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.25433-light-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-238d80dda721f3d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:light-heads" data-paper-title="Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-52edfaf206e2bd93">Can a new Light Heads objective improve the backbone after a stop-gradient on shared features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alight-heads">Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not through that loss path: it trains the shallow head but cannot update the shared backbone, reducing interference with existing tasks. Window resets make head training ages comparable but may sacrifice fit on sparse objectives. Gradient isolation and resets are separate; improved head AUC does not establish an improved backbone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Add a feedback head without harming a mature click tower; resetting weekly supports fair upstream comparisons but may leave a rare objective undertrained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25433">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.25433-light-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52edfaf206e2bd93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:light-heads" data-paper-title="Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfaadddfa74f0247">Why trade off training-age comparability against sparse fitting when resetting a Light Head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alight-heads">Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Resetting each window equalizes training age across upstream variants. Keeping the head preserves sparse label experience and may fit better. Short-window resets clearly regressed in the local source, so the right choice depends on the experimental goal and available data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A head trained three weeks versus a head trained one day confounds an upstream comparison. Reset both for a fairer comparison, but rare labels may not be enough to relearn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25433">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.25433-light-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfaadddfa74f0247">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:light-heads" data-paper-title="Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceefd5e0f0b3dc9c">What should be checked separately for Light Head gradient isolation and reset?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alight-heads">Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With only the new-task loss, shared θ must receive zero gradient while light-head ψ receives nonzero gradient. At a window boundary, reinitialize only ψ and preserve existing θ and main head φ as specified. Resetting does not imply isolation; do not erase backbone optimizer state accidentally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A changed shared parameter after the new-task update violates isolation. Resetting the main click head too would destroy the baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25433">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.25433-light-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceefd5e0f0b3dc9c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ts-prior" data-paper-title="LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-llm-ts-prior-97482120" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d04d3e08bb42ff94">Why turn LLM judgments into Beta pseudocounts instead of making direct recommendations in LLM-TS Prior?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ts-prior">LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER WEBTOON</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pseudocounts encode an initial success probability in a Bayesian state that feedback can update. Thompson sampling balances exploration, and real observations should be able to override the prior. Text can be biased and user clusters need not be homogeneous.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A favorable text judgment supplies a moderate prior for one group. Later clicks and skips correct it instead of the system recommending the item forever.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03382">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.03382-llm-ts-prior/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d04d3e08bb42ff94">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ts-prior" data-paper-title="LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff3deba117656c28">Why is prior strength κ as important as the probability p when turning an LLM judgment into Beta pseudocounts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ts-prior">LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER WEBTOON</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>p sets the initial preference and κ controls how much real feedback changes it. A large κ can let wrong semantics dominate for too long, while a tiny one barely helps cold start. Thompson sampling explores and updates the posterior, so the LLM is a starting point. A grouped local proxy does not establish general usefulness of text priors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two items start at 80%, but one prior represents a few observations and the other thousands. Repeated failures overturn the first much sooner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03382">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.03382-llm-ts-prior/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff3deba117656c28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ts-prior" data-paper-title="LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-914728a81f5028cf">Why do equal p and unequal κ produce different responses to early feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ts-prior">LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER WEBTOON</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>p determines the mean, while κ determines how much pseudo-evidence supports it. A stronger prior resists real observations, changing exploration even at the same mean. Too strong can lock in errors; too weak loses useful knowledge. No κ is universally better for all groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two 60% priors represent two and 200 observations. Three failures change the former far more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03382">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.03382-llm-ts-prior/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-914728a81f5028cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ts-prior" data-paper-title="LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-28b338121e35df01">Why distinguish prior pseudocounts from observed successes and failures when updating a Beta prior?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ts-prior">LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER WEBTOON</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Initialize parameters as 1+κp and 1+κ(1−p). Add counts only for arms actually shown and observed, and keep groups separate as specified. Future test feedback cannot initialize the prior. The local genre proxy does not prove actual LLM semantic calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unselected arm has no outcome this round. Counting it as a failure because another arm won distorts the posterior and suppresses exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03382">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.03382-llm-ts-prior/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28b338121e35df01">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mgoe" data-paper-title="Macro Graph of Experts for Billion-Scale Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mgoe-e3468d6f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4ad32d70416c198">Why build a Macro Task Merging Graph before expert propagation in MGOE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amgoe">Macro Graph of Experts for Billion-Scale Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph represents stable sharing relations that a per-sample gate does not explicitly encode. Macro Graph Bottom/Experts propagate information before task-specific towers. Relations can change across scenarios, and edges do not establish causality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click, watch time, and purchase can share information without implying clicks cause purchases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.10520-mgoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4ad32d70416c198">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mgoe" data-paper-title="Macro Graph of Experts for Billion-Scale Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7af4301a11225bf7">What does MGOE&#x27;s explicit task graph add to MMoE&#x27;s sample-level gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amgoe">Macro Graph of Experts for Billion-Scale Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sample-level mixtures do not explicitly encode stable task relationships. Graph bottom and experts propagate between related objectives before task towers, separating global structure from local routing. Wrong edges can propagate negative transfer. Compare related and unrelated tasks rather than assuming the graph is correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Clicks, cart additions, and purchases may share paths, while reports need other signals; the gate need not relearn every task relationship per sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.10520-mgoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7af4301a11225bf7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mgoe" data-paper-title="Macro Graph of Experts for Billion-Scale Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d46d50e1c7231b58">What additional sharing bias does MGOE introduce relative to independent MMoE task gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amgoe">Macro Graph of Experts for Billion-Scale Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MMoE shares experts implicitly by example. MGOE adds graph-constrained task propagation, which can help sparse objectives or transmit wrong relations. Overall gains and changed head share do not establish all-task improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A sparse purchase task can borrow click knowledge; a mistakenly connected returns task may inherit the wrong direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.10520-mgoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d46d50e1c7231b58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mgoe" data-paper-title="Macro Graph of Experts for Billion-Scale Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f0b168dfe442d78">Why align MGOE&#x27;s normalized adjacency and task indices with expert tensors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amgoe">Macro Graph of Experts for Billion-Scale Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rows and columns of A identify nodes and task towers must read the correct propagated rows of H. Normalization, self-loops, and depth determine mixing. Use labels only in training; do not rebuild the graph from test feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A purchase node paired with watch-time features still multiplies correctly but shares the wrong information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.10520-mgoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f0b168dfe442d78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mmoe" data-paper-title="Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mmoe-a1bda9df" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7894d7d31049945b">Does sharing experts but keeping private gates make MMoE tasks independent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ammoe">Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Shared expert gradients still transmit effects between tasks. Private gates change expert weights and task heads produce separate outputs. This lies between full sharing and full separation. Check actual routes and task results for specialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click and purchase use the same price expert at different rates; click training still changes the expert that purchase reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7894d7d31049945b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mmoe" data-paper-title="Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad97f0b0fdf40ae7">Why can shared experts with task-specific gates in MMoE reduce shared-bottom negative transfer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ammoe">Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared bottom forces one intermediate representation and can mix conflicting gradients. MMoE lets each task conditionally combine jointly trained experts, sharing useful parts while selecting different mixtures. It enables soft specialization but does not guarantee interpretable experts or eliminate conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click and purchase can both use category knowledge while one emphasizes novelty and the other price.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad97f0b0fdf40ae7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mmoe" data-paper-title="Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-08ebd1aca483e5d1">What trade-off does MMoE offer between a shared bottom and independent task networks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ammoe">Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared bottom returns one representation, independent networks share no parameters, and MMoE offers several common experts combined per task. Extra experts add flexibility, computation, and collapse risk. Task relationships and data determine whether the compromise helps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two tasks can share interest features but differ elsewhere. Unrelated tasks may suffer from sharing, while scarce data can make independent models unstable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08ebd1aca483e5d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mmoe" data-paper-title="Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6a76388ad05af8a">Why normalize MMoE gates across experts, and how many sets of weights do four experts and two tasks need?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ammoe">Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each task has a distinct four-weight distribution per sample and combines same-space expert outputs. Normalizing across tasks makes them compete for one budget and changes the algorithm. The four-expert, two-head local control is shared-bottom.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click and purchase each need four weights summing to one; normalizing all eight together couples them incorrectly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6a76388ad05af8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pa-bridge" data-paper-title="Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pa-bridge-6df7bc67" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a068573604e1dba">Why isn&#x27;t PA-Bridge passive-to-active transfer just rewriting browsed titles as questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apa-bridge">Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Active queries express actions and problems absent from passive views. Align distributions, then use semantic codes and weights to reduce exposure loops. A question mark cannot create user intent, and model inference is not an explicit request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;How do I exercise?&#x27; rewrites a title but may miss the actual question about protecting a knee.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05855-pa-bridge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a068573604e1dba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pa-bridge" data-paper-title="Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9bfad439e3d5eb0">Why align passive browsing to active queries before discretization and reweighting in PA-Bridge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apa-bridge">Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Browsing says what was seen, while active queries express what users want to ask. Direct reuse can suggest familiar but poor conversation starters. Distribution alignment bridges intent spaces, and discrete units with reweighting reduce repeated dominance by popular exposures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Frequent fitness videos may coexist with a specific need to ask about training with knee discomfort; query alignment can surface the latter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05855-pa-bridge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9bfad439e3d5eb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pa-bridge" data-paper-title="Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb10a75c8320e802">How does PA-Bridge reweighting differ from selecting the most-browsed topic?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apa-bridge">Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Counts reflect prior exposure, so top frequency reinforces what was already shown. Reweighting reduces dominant semantic units and broadens active topics, but too much favors irrelevant tail content. Diversity is not satisfaction or causal debiasing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reweighting can surface related strength training alongside common weight-loss content, not justify arbitrary unrelated topics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pa-bridge" data-paper-title="Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4276e4fc92ccc22a">What temporal constraint applies when fitting PA-Bridge hpassive to hactive pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apa-bridge">Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use active queries as training targets and cut passive context before the query. Codes and weights must also use allowed history. The public proxy lacks genuine active-query logs, so an Align function alone does not demonstrate cross-behavior transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rehab videos watched after asking about a knee cannot be part of the prefix used to predict that question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.05855-pa-bridge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4276e4fc92ccc22a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pearl-percentile" data-paper-title="PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pearl-percentile-dbf6d244" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-60a85dba32ab471e">Why identify PEARL&#x27;s reference distribution when reporting a percentile?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apearl-percentile">PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A percentile is the fraction of reference outcomes exceeded, so users, context, and windows change its meaning. More comparisons reduce sampling noise, and value weights connect goals. Relative rank does not remove logging bias or prove causal incrementality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Thirty seconds can be high for short clips and low for long tutorials; a wrong reference reverses interpretation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21752">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.21752-pearl-percentile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-60a85dba32ab471e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pearl-percentile" data-paper-title="PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4447b64d4565cd98">Why estimate PEARL percentiles via repeated comparisons rather than regress raw behaviors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apearl-percentile">PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw values differ in scale and bias. Comparing a behavior against references estimates its relative position, with more independent comparisons reducing variance. Value weighting and long-term co-training connect objectives. Percentiles depend on the reference and are not causally debiased value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Thirty seconds means different things for a 15-second clip and a ten-minute video; compare within suitable references.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21752">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.21752-pearl-percentile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4447b64d4565cd98">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pearl-percentile" data-paper-title="PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8375492d01fdaa2">How do repeated pairwise comparisons trade scale and variance against raw-label regression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apearl-percentile">PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Regression preserves units but is sensitive to extremes. Comparisons organize relative position across scales but lose absolute gaps and introduce sampling error. Under independence, larger N reduces variance; bootstrap does not remove systematic bias. Neither objective is universally superior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: 100 and 101 seconds can differ in percentile despite a small raw gap, while a huge anomaly no longer dominates linearly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21752">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.21752-pearl-percentile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8375492d01fdaa2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pearl-percentile" data-paper-title="PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b544a9feebc5aa13">Why check dependence among PEARL comparisons before using p(1−p)/N?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apearl-percentile">PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The expression assumes appropriate Bernoulli comparisons and sampling. Repeated or correlated references do not add N independent observations. Record weights, bootstrap, and co-training provenance; sampling variance is not training variance. Do not use test references to choose targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Comparing the same video 100 times does not reduce uncertainty tenfold as 100 independent references might.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21752">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.21752-pearl-percentile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b544a9feebc5aa13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinequalizer" data-paper-title="PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pinequalizer-1595745d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c43ee2f671ca7474">Why treat PinEqualizer exploration as both a supply and a model problem?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinequalizer">PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New items can disappear in corpus, retrieval, or ranking. Content reduces dependence on old interactions, an exploration corpus allows entry, and uncertainty allocates feedback. Stage survival locates bottlenecks; a high fresh quota does not guarantee relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A favorable ranker cannot recommend an item that retrieval never includes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.22518-pinequalizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c43ee2f671ca7474">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinequalizer" data-paper-title="PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ad2cb9fa87f3c82">Why check fresh-content survival at every stage in PinEqualizer instead of boosting it only in fine ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinequalizer">PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Items filtered in corpus or retrieval never reach the ranker. Track stage inputs and survival to locate bottlenecks. Content features, interaction dropout, and calibration reduce dependence on old exposure; separate exploration and uncertainty rewards collect feedback. Relevance still constrains exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A new recipe filtered before retrieval cannot benefit from a ranking boost. Preserve entry and explore promising items selectively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.22518-pinequalizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ad2cb9fa87f3c82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinequalizer" data-paper-title="PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a636a4fd426b06ff">Why does PinEqualizer UCB consider uncertainty and relevance instead of merely lowering popular scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinequalizer">PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Popularity penalties do not identify worthwhile unknown items. UCB promotes low-exposure or uncertain items, with search relevance limiting unrelated exploration. Locally fresh exposure rose but overall NDCG fell, so report both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Explore a relevant new recipe, not unrelated news just because it is obscure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.22518-pinequalizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a636a4fd426b06ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinequalizer" data-paper-title="PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-429c749e92f0ed36">Why preserve validation&#x27;s UCB α=0 rather than tune α for a better fresh metric?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinequalizer">PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Validation rejected extra exploration under the current objective. Do not reselect on test. The debiased model itself can raise fresh exposure without UCB. Report freshness denominators and overall regression instead of changing objectives afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the model already increases fresh impressions severalfold and UCB hurts relevance, do not force α above zero to claim bandit use.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.22518-pinequalizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-429c749e92f0ed36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ple" data-paper-title="Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ple-a2bf42a4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0451f6496f52aa1f">Why can average task AUC hide PLE&#x27;s seesaw effect?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aple">Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One task can improve while another regresses and the average obscures the loser. Report each objective under the same joint training. This differs from measurement noise and does not require identical gains across tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click AUC gains two points and purchase loses one; average AUC rises without both improving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1145/3383313.3412236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/recsys2020-ple-ple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0451f6496f52aa1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ple" data-paper-title="Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3abbb3ea731757ca">Why does PLE distinguish shared and private experts beyond MMoE&#x27;s task-specific gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aple">Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MMoE mixes differently but all experts receive multiple tasks&#x27; gradients. PLE reserves private capacity alongside shared experts and extracts common and task-specific information layerwise. This changes information and gradient paths at extra capacity and routing cost; verify whether regressions actually decline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Share category interest while purchase-private experts learn affordability and click-private experts learn headline appeal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1145/3383313.3412236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/recsys2020-ple-ple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3abbb3ea731757ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ple" data-paper-title="Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cfe1ebe206d5bfb">Why isn&#x27;t PLE just increasing MMoE expert count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aple">Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More shared experts still accept all tasks&#x27; gradients. PLE changes access and gradient topology with private groups and layered fusion, not just parameter count. Match budgets and do not generalize a local two-task comparison to every conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ten additional shared experts can still transmit click interference to purchases; a purchase-private group blocks that route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1145/3383313.3412236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/recsys2020-ple-ple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cfe1ebe206d5bfb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ple" data-paper-title="Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-433f6282251197a2">Why restrict each PLE task gate to its private experts and shared experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aple">Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>This is the CGC separation contract. Accessing another task&#x27;s private group changes the topology. Verify expert identities, masks, actual gradients, and next-layer channel layout rather than trusting variable names.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Concatenating all experts without a mask can preserve output shape but let click read purchase-private features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1145/3383313.3412236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/recsys2020-ple-ple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-433f6282251197a2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
