<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:podcast-mtl" data-paper-title="Cold-Starting Podcast Ads and Promotions with Multi-Task Learning on Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-podcast-mtl-fc67da12" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce83c5c320e4d33e">Does cold start in Podcast MTL mean no content or no target feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apodcast-mtl">Cold-Starting Podcast Ads and Promotions with Multi-Task Learning on Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The gap is ad click/play labels for new podcasts, not necessarily missing titles or topics. Shared content and context help without representing observed ad outcomes. Transfer supplies a training signal, not a real click log.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A show&#x27;s host and description can suggest likely audiences before exposure, but cannot verify their ad clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02306">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.02306-podcast-mtl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce83c5c320e4d33e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:podcast-mtl" data-paper-title="Cold-Starting Podcast Ads and Promotions with Multi-Task Learning on Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf5d9b50db60650a">How does Podcast MTL use organic promotion for cold ads, and why balance gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apodcast-mtl">Cold-Starting Podcast Ads and Promotions with Multi-Task Learning on Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User, content, and context representations share abundant organic signals while separate heads preserve objectives. Sample and gradient imbalance can drown the sparse advertising task, so adjust contributions. Transfer can fail when tasks differ; sharing does not guarantee gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A new podcast has organic plays but no ad clicks. Learn audience clues in the shared encoder while preventing organic gradients from overwhelming ad supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02306">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.02306-podcast-mtl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf5d9b50db60650a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:podcast-mtl" data-paper-title="Cold-Starting Podcast Ads and Promotions with Multi-Task Learning on Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c78cd2c217eacbf6">How does gradient balancing treat a small podcast task differently from mixing by counts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apodcast-mtl">Cold-Starting Podcast Ads and Promotions with Multi-Task Learning on Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Counts let the large task dominate shared weights. Balancing actual contributions preserves the sparse ad direction, but too much can amplify noise. Evaluate per task; duplicating records cannot guarantee cold-start gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One million organic and one thousand ad examples can bury ad gradients. Moderate balancing does not mean infinitely upweighting a single ad label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02306">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.02306-podcast-mtl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c78cd2c217eacbf6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:podcast-mtl" data-paper-title="Cold-Starting Podcast Ads and Promotions with Multi-Task Learning on Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6cb40b601772ffa9">Why not fill missing Podcast MTL labels with zeros?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apodcast-mtl">Cold-Starting Podcast Ads and Promotions with Multi-Task Learning on Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An organic example may never expose the ad, so its ad response is unobserved, not negative. Mask that loss; observed objectives can still train shared features. Record task identity, data construction, and α. Movies proxy for podcasts only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Listening after organic exposure does not imply the user ignored an unseen ad.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02306">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.02306-podcast-mtl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6cb40b601772ffa9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:promptshift" data-paper-title="Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-promptshift-7e539145" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-12d0a4e2ffd1606c">Does high PromptShift Drift directly imply lower accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apromptshift">Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Drift measures list change, not relevance of old and new items. SliceShift adds popularity direction, not quality. Independent relevance or feedback is needed; do not relabel sensitivity as accuracy loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Swapping two equally suitable films changes rank drift without necessarily hurting the user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34229">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.34229-promptshift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12d0a4e2ffd1606c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:promptshift" data-paper-title="Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-27ec4d2dd288c79e">Why hold history fixed and vary only identity prompts in PromptShift, then measure Drift and SliceShift separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apromptshift">Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing both confounds actual preference and identity cues. Drift measures overlap/rank changes and SliceShift measures cohort popularity direction; mainstreamness conditions relevance and inverse-popularity blending. This is a controlled sensitivity diagnostic, not causal discrimination proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Use the same movie history with and without identity text to see whether rankings shift toward cohort-popular films.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34229">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.34229-promptshift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27ec4d2dd288c79e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:promptshift" data-paper-title="Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fd0165111d28e58">Where does user conditioning enter adaptive inverse-popularity blending versus a uniform tail bonus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apromptshift">Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mainstreamness m changes the mix of relevance and inverse popularity, unlike a uniform bonus. Both can hurt relevance. Diagnostics do not establish real fairness or satisfaction and do not belong on formal capability leaderboards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A mainstream user and a niche user may need different corrections; pushing even more obscurity can be unhelpful for the latter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34229">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.34229-promptshift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fd0165111d28e58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:promptshift" data-paper-title="Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc6ed8a8ddc8268a">What must stay fixed between PromptShift&#x27;s reference and identity-prompt lists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apromptshift">Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep history, candidates, model, and decoding as consistent as possible and vary the identity cue only. Handle shared item ranks and set changes as defined; do not pair disjoint items artificially. Do not choose mitigation on test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If one arm also has recent clicks, drift may come from the extra behavior rather than identity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34229">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.34229-promptshift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc6ed8a8ddc8268a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ramp" data-paper-title="RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ramp-9687450e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-917b7d6f5d4a1bc0">Does RAMP&#x27;s non-personalized branch predict the same thing for every request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aramp">RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Center / University College Dublin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It can use ad content, public attributes, and request context without restricted personal fields. Constant output would discard allowed evidence. Follow permissions and do not disguise personal IDs as public.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rain gear on a rainy day and food on a sunny day can score differently without private browsing history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17473">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17473-ramp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-917b7d6f5d4a1bc0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ramp" data-paper-title="RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-228f5bd4932e7220">Why keep a separate RAMP path for unavailable personalization instead of filling zeros?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aramp">RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Center / University College Dublin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zeros conflate unavailable features with true zeros and force one representation across distinct inputs. An availability mask selects personalized or public paths, and training distills rich predictions to the restricted path. Serving remains limited to permitted features and cannot recover hidden personal history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unconsented request uses content and context, while authorized training examples can provide soft supervision without exposing restricted fields online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17473">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17473-ramp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-228f5bd4932e7220">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ramp" data-paper-title="RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee66fd4cfb400d2b">What does RAMP distillation add beyond training on missing features alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aramp">RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Center / University College Dublin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Missing-feature training uses hard labels. A rich teacher adds soft relational judgments, but student inputs may not recover all information and bias can transfer. A large relative gain over a tiny local baseline is not definitive industrial robustness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A teacher can distinguish two ads with similar public features; a student may learn a trend but cannot distinguish every user without public clues.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17473">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17473-ramp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee66fd4cfb400d2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ramp" data-paper-title="RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d20381b7e2ac0bfd">Why derive RAMP availability masks from actual permissions rather than prediction quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aramp">RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Center / University College Dublin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mask expresses feature access, not labels or which branch wins afterward. Distill on authorized samples and keep restricted test traffic free of personal features. Distinguish unavailable values from legitimate zeros.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Selecting the private branch only when a purchase occurs leaks outcomes. Use permission and field availability at request time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17473">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17473-ramp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d20381b7e2ac0bfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:scalr" data-paper-title="Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-scalr-f567c58a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c660befc3863b6da">Do SCALR translated target events actually occur?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ascalr">Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They are conditional samples for downstream training, not exposures, clicks, or conversions. Keep synthetic identity and weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generating a target-domain training click on B from a source event on A does not create an audit fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00282">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.00282-scalr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c660befc3863b6da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:scalr" data-paper-title="Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e2a137aa9d4e7ec">Why synthesize events and sample targets instead of always taking top-k?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ascalr">Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Estimate target distributions from overlap and emit ordinary training records for different models. Sampling retains tail opportunities rather than repeating head products, without claiming the records occurred.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Travel browsing may synthesize adapters or organizers, not only the highest-probability suitcase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00282">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.00282-scalr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e2a137aa9d4e7ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:scalr" data-paper-title="Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-87ad21447ca81b7c">How does data-level transfer differ from adding cross-domain modules to each model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ascalr">Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Synthetic events reuse the ordinary target training interface. Model-level transfer is tied to architecture. Shared interfaces ease reuse but do not guarantee equal effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several rankers can share events rather than each implementing a special attention module.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00282">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.00282-scalr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87ad21447ca81b7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:scalr" data-paper-title="Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-757eb29377c39af1">What isolation does conditional SCALR estimation need?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ascalr">Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Estimate co-occurrence from overlapping train users, not target test events; handle zero denominators and missing coverage. Genre proxies are not Meta conversions or CVR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading test purchases before building translation probabilities leaks future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00282">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.00282-scalr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-757eb29377c39af1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:smes" data-paper-title="SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-smes-9171fefe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a1f6aeebf107665">Why use both shared and private experts in SMES?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asmes">SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stable shared experts hold common signals, task-private experts preserve differences, and global load balances cross-task dispatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Viewing and buying share interest features but can retain distinct decision experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09386">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09386-smes/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a1f6aeebf107665">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:smes" data-paper-title="SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ed4c7004f28e1f0">Why combine fixed shared activation, adaptive private experts, and global balance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asmes">SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared capacity handles commonality, private routing handles task differences, and global balance detects concentration hidden within tasks. Actual specialization and balance penalties still require evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clicks and purchases can share interest experts while choosing novelty or price specialists, unless global dispatch overloads one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09386">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09386-smes/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ed4c7004f28e1f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:smes" data-paper-title="SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0beb83b4a61eb35">How do shared/private pools differ from one MoE router?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asmes">SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate pools constrain common and task-specific selections; one pool lets all compete. This does not guarantee less negative transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reserving all shared capacity for purchases can harm other tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09386">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09386-smes/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0beb83b4a61eb35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:smes" data-paper-title="SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-de54a8bdf45919c6">Can balancing be computed separately per task only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asmes">SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Separate balance can miss aggregate expert overload. Use cross-task counts. MovieLens lacks production sparse scheduling, so dispatch counts are not throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Individually spread tasks can all favor the same two experts globally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09386">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09386-smes/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de54a8bdf45919c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twice" data-paper-title="TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-twice-bd9f2dd2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-62772935573ba6cb">Why distinguish not-yet-converted from never-converting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwice">TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A recent click can convert later. Final CVR times delay CDF describes current observation without treating immature negatives as permanent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Today&#x27;s click can become tomorrow&#x27;s order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25404-twice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62772935573ba6cb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twice" data-paper-title="TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-90f01d7ee97d595c">Why learn final conversion and delay CDF separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwice">TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An unobserved conversion may be delayed. Event probability times delay CDF gives observable status. Two clocks/windows address maturity bias, subject to a suitable delay model. Public timestamps are not ad results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five minutes without purchase is not equivalent to a week without purchase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25404-twice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90f01d7ee97d595c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twice" data-paper-title="TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb053d77c23dd08a">What do click-clock status and conversion-clock delay measure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwice">TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One measures maturity since click, the other the conversion delay distribution. Joint windows correct observation bias; one clock can mix event likelihood with timing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal waits can differ in label maturity under different sampling windows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25404-twice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb053d77c23dd08a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twice" data-paper-title="TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e0c01dbb4d8dde1">What monotonic boundary must the delay CDF satisfy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwice">TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stay in [0,1] and never decrease with time. Keep it separate from final CVR. Public proxies lack actual ad delay, aggregates, and revenue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A two-day CDF cannot fall below the one-day value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25404-twice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e0c01dbb4d8dde1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twitch-mor" data-paper-title="Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-twitch-mor-68bc3da8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf5fda6b62b7980b">Why distinguish immediate and delayed feedback in Twitch ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwitch-mor">Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Twitch</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Views and interactions appear fast, while follows and payments may mature later. Lifecycle groups also value objectives differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new viewer who has not paid yet is not an immediate negative for value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.04455-twitch-mor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf5fda6b62b7980b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twitch-mor" data-paper-title="Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a6f243fe269c1c1">Why handle delays, lifecycle weighting, and MMoE gates together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwitch-mor">Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Twitch</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Outcomes differ in observation time and user stage. Immediate/delayed models address labels, segments encode objectives, and MMoE shares/selects experts. Overall metrics cannot prove all groups improve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Support viewing habits for new users and deeper engagement for established users without letting immediate clicks dominate delayed payment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.04455-twitch-mor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a6f243fe269c1c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twitch-mor" data-paper-title="Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8aaac58d9bd49b60">Are MMoE gates and segment weights at the same level?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwitch-mor">Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Twitch</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gates select expert mixtures per task; segment weights alter task contribution. One global weight does not implement expert interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>New users can emphasize viewing while each task still has a different expert mixture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.04455-twitch-mor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8aaac58d9bd49b60">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twitch-mor" data-paper-title="Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb40c9610249d15e">Does local Twitch-MOR explain production gains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwitch-mor">Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Twitch</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It lacks private features, mature delay labels, and traffic. Fix segments and maturity windows; never define segments using future test payments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Labeling future payers as currently high value leaks outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.04455-twitch-mor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb40c9610249d15e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unimvt" data-paper-title="Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unimvt-218d40bb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-490ec6066f4cd35b">Why separate baseline click propensity and coupon-strength sensitivity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunimvt">Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Users may buy anyway. Separate natural propensity from treatment response to estimate increment rather than conversion under a coupon.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A coupon used by someone who would buy anyway does not necessarily generate a sale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12972-unimvt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-490ec6066f4cd35b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unimvt" data-paper-title="Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c56d597faaf6232">Why separate baseline and coupon sensitivity before comparing predictions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunimvt">Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Natural propensity can masquerade as coupon gain. Two towers model baseline/treatment; counterfactual constraints link unobserved cases, and unit uplift normalizes tier increments. Identification still depends on assignment and assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A naturally 80%-likely buyer may gain less than one moving 20%→50%, subject to selection bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12972-unimvt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c56d597faaf6232">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unimvt" data-paper-title="Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c31b90b9a26fcc65">Why isn&#x27;t treatment CTR uplift?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunimvt">Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uplift compares treated and untreated potential outcomes under matched conditions; high treated CTR can reflect selection. Counterfactual identification needs assumptions, not just two predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Coupons targeted to high-intent users can show high CTR without causing it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12972-unimvt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c31b90b9a26fcc65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unimvt" data-paper-title="Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d47d70a6e230f86c">Does local UniMVT have randomized coupon tiers and counterfactuals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunimvt">Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens checks two-tower and counterfactual constraints only. Causal estimates require overlap and confounding control; test outcomes must not define treatment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Assigning coupons by rating leaks outcomes into group assignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kl-mopd" data-paper-title="KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kl-mopd-35d8ffea" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-225530c49babcf34">Why estimate each teacher&#x27;s difficulty at each SID position in KL-MOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akl-mopd">KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An item ID needs several correct tokens. The click teacher may be easy to imitate early and the value teacher later. Fixed half weights ignore this; KL-MOPD upweights the harder teacher based on each initial student-to-teacher KL gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A three-part code starts with category and ends with attributes. If a teacher diverges only on category, one sequence-wide weight obscures that difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36973-kl-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-225530c49babcf34">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kl-mopd" data-paper-title="KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd274eb36d8c0d0d">Does KL-MOPD compute alpha from the current student or the frozen initial student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akl-mopd">KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calibrate once before training using the frozen initial student&#x27;s own sampled prefixes. Training loss uses current student prefixes but does not recalculate alpha from current gaps. Dynamic weights would define a different objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Initial gaps 1 and 3 produce fixed weights 1/4 and 3/4. Later gaps of 2 and 1 do not swap them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36973-kl-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd274eb36d8c0d0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kl-mopd" data-paper-title="KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1b61ee586eb6c08">Is weighting two reverse KL losses equivalent to averaging teacher probabilities and computing one KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akl-mopd">KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not in general. Weight the separate student-to-teacher KL losses, not an arithmetic mixture of teacher probabilities, and keep KL(student||teacher), not forward KL. Negative controls distinguish the computations without establishing recommendation gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Teachers favor different tokens. An arithmetic mixture keeps mass on both modes; weighted reverse KL involves log teacher probabilities and yields different gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36973-kl-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1b61ee586eb6c08">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kl-mopd" data-paper-title="KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f943ef4c424b8aa8">Why doesn&#x27;t a gradient-tested tensor loss establish on-policy recommender training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akl-mopd">KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logits alone don&#x27;t tell the kernel who sampled a prefix. Initial calibration, current student generation, frozen teacher scoring, SID decoding and real splits require external integration. Only the loss component and small CPU/CUDA mechanism evidence are present.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The kernel accepts cached old-policy prefixes, but that does not make them samples from the current student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36973-kl-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f943ef4c424b8aa8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

Which probability or value can observed clicks and conversions supervise?

## Takeaway

Define labels before architecture. ESMM separates post-impression click probability, post-click conversion, and their joint event. MMoE shares experts with task-specific gates. PLE separates shared from task-private information. Duration, delayed conversion, exposure selection, and attribution change what supervision means. Pseudo-labels and set rewards need justification. Causal lift asks a counterfactual question not answered by prediction accuracy.

## Example

With 1,000 impressions, CTR 10%, and post-click CVR 20%, joint click-and-conversion probability is 2%, or about 20 conversions. A new policy cannot claim all 20; some users would have purchased anyway.

## Common pitfall

Sharing tasks does not remove selection bias. Treating unclicked examples as CVR negatives confuses conditional and joint probabilities. Delay, missing features, and exposure are not one noise source. Verify each observation assumption; synthetic labels support only mechanism checks.

## Reading order

Use ESMM to establish funnel probabilities, MMoE for task-specific selection of shared experts, and PLE for private paths under conflict. All train locally on public constructed tasks, not real ad funnels.

1. [Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate](../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931)
2. [Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts](../../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/)
3. [Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2020-ple-ple/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3383313.3412236)

## Check your understanding

CTR rises from 10% to 20% and post-click CVR stays at 20%, doubling joint conversion to 4%. Does this prove better CVR or causal lift?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Neither follows. CTR alone can double the joint rate while conditional CVR stays unchanged. Causal lift still requires a credible control or identification assumptions.

</details>
